name: Hwana
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists (Kraft 1981 Chadic Wordlists II), ethnography and overviews for Hwana; no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2022. Comprehensive Bibliography of Chadic and Hausa Linguistics, 5th edition. Bloomington: IUScholarWorks.
sources.note: Bibliography only. Keyword 'Hona' attached to exactly two entries: Frajzyngier 1985b 'Causative and benefactive in Chadic' (Afrika und Übersee 68: 23-42; syntax) and Kraft 1981 Chadic Wordlists. No grammar, phonology or sketch of Hwana/Hona listed.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The Reconstruction of the Phonology and Lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the Linguistic History of the Central Chadic Languages. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Hwana appears only in classification tables and cognate sets; data source listed as 'Hwana [hwo] Tera (Harley n.d.) Word list (unpublished)'. Abstract and Section III intro state the reconstruction is done 'not including tone or stress' / 'No attempt has been made to reconstruct tone or stress.' No Hwana-specific prosodic statement.

sources.citation: lexibank/kraftchadic: CLDF dataset derived from Kraft 1981 Chadic Wordlists (Tresoldi, List, Cysouw, Bouda). Row 'Hwona, hwan1240, hwo'.
sources.note: Digitised wordlist forms only (tone-marked); Kraft's prose notes are not included.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record hwan1240 and reference list (Meek 1931, Temple 1922, Kraft 1981, Haruna 2005, Kropp Dakubu (ed.) 1977 WALDS, all overview/wordlist/ethnographic).
sources.note: No grammar, grammar sketch or phonology registered (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages (2020 edition). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation / author.
sources.note: Entry 181 Hwana (Hona, Hwona; Gombi LGA, Guyuk + 30 villages; Tera group): references = 'Wordlist: Kraft (1981)' only. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Osaji, Bede. 1979. Language Survey in Nigeria. CIRB Publication B-81. Québec: Laval (ERIC microfiche).
sources.note: Index entry only: 'Hwana. Gongola State, Adamawa Division, Ga'anda District. Chadic: Central: Tera group: Eastern.' No description.

sources.note: Orthography statements for Nigerian Chadic languages routinely state whether tone and stress are contrastive and how they are (not) written; would be the most likely place for an explicit first-hand stress statement.
